name: Persistent mode
interaction: Choose IN or OUT and keep that direction armed across scans. A label immediately submits the chosen movement.
functional_difference: The current plan's persistent direction with whole-stack default; scope is explicit and resets to stack after a confirmed movement.
benefit: Fast when an operator processes a continuous run in one direction.
risk: The previous operator's direction may remain armed. A large persistent direction indicator is essential. Repeat scans remain no-ops rather than toggles.
backend_change: None beyond the planned movement endpoint and same-request reconciliation.

name: Reset after scan
interaction: Arm a direction for one movement; confirmed success returns the station to an unarmed state.
functional_difference: Requires a fresh direction choice before every subsequent movement, instead of retaining or automatically resetting to IN.
benefit: Reduces inherited direction mistakes between operators.
risk: Adds a touch per stack. Resetting to an unarmed state is deliberate; an automatic opposite direction or default-IN reset could make an accidental repeat a real movement.
backend_change: Client workflow only. Existing movement/idempotency rules remain necessary.

name: Scan then act
interaction: Read the label, inspect current locations, then press Check IN or Check OUT.
functional_difference: A scan performs lookup only. The direction action submits the movement after its identity is visible.
benefit: The operator sees the identified stack before choosing what should happen.
risk: One extra interaction per movement; a retained preview must be clearly tied to the next action.
backend_change: Uses planned lookup followed by movement; no new server capability.

name: Guided movement
interaction: Direction, label, scope/review, explicit confirmation, receipt.
functional_difference: Separates every decision into a sequential stage and supports numbered selection in the review stage.
benefit: Makes the order clear for students and infrequent operators.
risk: Slower for experienced operators; returning to an earlier stage must discard stale selections.
backend_change: Client workflow using existing lookup, versions, and movement endpoint.

name: Dedicated lanes
device: Two scanners or two dedicated physical stations
interaction: Entry scanner always records IN; exit scanner always records OUT.
functional_difference: Direction comes from scanner/station identity rather than a shared touch mode.
benefit: Removes the direction choice when physical traffic is separated.
risk: Two ordinary USB keyboard/HID scanners cannot inherently be distinguished by a browser. This requires separate stations, programmed prefixes, or a native capture service; labels must not be scanned in the wrong lane.
backend_change: Dedicated stations already fit the endpoint. Distinguishing two scanners in one browser needs device routing or a native/prefix bridge.

name: Scanner command cards
device: Scanner-only station with small status display
interaction: Scan printed mode/scope command cards, then specimen labels; numbered-selection and acknowledgment cards handle exceptions.
functional_difference: Moves mode, scope, selection, and early-exit acknowledgment into scannable commands, avoiding required touch input.
benefit: Works with gloves and scanner-only hardware.
risk: Command labels must be visually distinct and validated. The operator still needs a readable display for exact selection and incomplete-conditioning warnings.
backend_change: Client command parser, reserved command namespace, and configuration for printed cards; movement API can remain unchanged.

name: Physical direction buttons
device: Pi + USB scanner + external button unit
interaction: Press a large physical direction button, then scan a specimen. The signal is consumed after confirmation.
functional_difference: Direction is armed by GPIO/HID hardware rather than an on-screen control.
benefit: Tactile operation with gloves and less touchscreen dependence.
risk: Requires a local hardware bridge, reliable button debouncing, and visible armed-direction feedback; disconnected hardware must never leave an invisible armed state.
backend_change: Local GPIO/HID event bridge sends direction intent to the client; existing movement endpoint can be reused.

name: State-suggested action
interaction: Read current location, review the proposed opposite movement, explicitly confirm it.
functional_difference: Derives a proposed direction from recorded state but never moves on scan alone. Mixed groups require an exact selection.
benefit: Avoids an inherited direction mode and makes current state visible.
risk: A repeat lookup after success proposes the opposite action. Explicit confirmation is mandatory; an automatic state toggle would be unsafe with repeated scans or stale location records.
backend_change: Existing lookup and versioned movement endpoint; suggestion logic belongs in the client.

name: Room inventory board
interaction: Select specimen tiles under Inside or Outside, or scan a stack to select it; apply a movement to the exact selection.
functional_difference: Organizes actions around current location and explicit specimen selection rather than scanner direction mode.
benefit: Makes partial movements and mixed stacks easy to see.
risk: Twenty specimens fit; real rooms with many stacks need search/grouping. Selected specimens spanning different locations are rejected rather than silently filtered.
backend_change: Current stack-detail and selection movement APIs are sufficient for this bounded design; a full room inventory view would need an efficient inventory query.

name: Numbered specimen grid
device: Landscape touchscreen for frequent partial checkout
interaction: Choose exact numbered specimens, select direction, confirm the selection. An individual label adds its specimen to the selection.
functional_difference: Exact selection is the primary workflow instead of the exception to whole-stack scanning.
benefit: Fast and auditable when operators usually remove only a few specimens.
risk: Selection must not persist invisibly between unrelated stacks; all selected IDs and versions must be checked atomically.
backend_change: Existing selected-specimen movement capability; preserve version checks and all-or-none updates.

name: Individual scan basket
device: USB scanner + compact touch or desktop screen
interaction: Scan individual specimens into a deduplicated basket, then confirm one movement for the basket.
functional_difference: Several label scans define the exact movement scope without tapping specimen numbers.
benefit: The physical specimens in hand directly define the selection.
risk: An accidentally added specimen needs a visible removal control. v1 only permits specimens from one fixed stack; cross-stack baskets need a larger backend contract.
backend_change: Existing selected-ID API for a single stack. Cross-stack basket batching would require a new atomic batch endpoint.

name: Multi-stack staging tray
interaction: Scan several fixed stacks onto a staging tray and confirm their combined movement once.
functional_difference: Processes cotton's 20 specimens and nylon's 12 as one reviewed simulated batch.
benefit: Reduces repeated confirmation work for a cart of stacks.
risk: Atomicity across multiple stacks is a new requirement. A failure or mixed-location stack must reject the whole batch, and an uncertain response must reconcile one batch request.
backend_change: New transactional multi-stack batch endpoint with shared request identity, per-stack versions, exact scope, and batch-level early-exit acknowledgment; the existing single-stack endpoint does not provide this behavior.

name: Destination token pairing
interaction: Read a destination token and a specimen label in either order, then confirm their pairing.
functional_difference: The room/outside token supplies destination intent rather than a preconfigured persistent station direction.
benefit: Portable operation can make the destination explicit without navigating a room selector.
risk: Room tokens can be confused or copied; checkout still must match the room currently holding every selected specimen.
backend_change: Token namespace and room/station mapping in the client; a truly roaming station needs authenticated destination authorization and station identity policy.

name: Handheld camera
interaction: Capture a label, choose whole-stack or individual scope, choose direction, confirm.
functional_difference: Uses a camera capture/review cycle with thumb-reachable controls rather than USB HID typing.
benefit: Useful when the operator has no fixed workstation or dedicated scanner.
risk: Real camera access and QR decoding need secure-context/browser support, suitable lighting, and readable labels. This prototype does not request camera access.
backend_change: Camera/QR client integration; existing lookup and movement endpoint can remain unchanged.

name: Minimal scanner console
interaction: Submit an explicit IN + label or OUT + label command; exact-selection and ACK commands handle exceptions.
functional_difference: Direction travels with each command, avoiding a retained mode; the display focuses on plain-text request and receipt state.
benefit: Compact and predictable for trained users or programmable scanners.
risk: Ordinary specimen labels do not contain a direction. A prefix-programmed scanner, command bridge, or operator command entry is required; error states must remain readable.
backend_change: Local combined-command parser or device bridge; planned movement API receives parsed explicit direction and scope.

name: Operator badge then scan
interaction: Identify a named operator before choosing direction and scanning a specimen; lock the station when finished.
functional_difference: Routine movements are attributed to a person instead of only to the room station.
benefit: Adds operator accountability and can tailor permissions or operator defaults.
risk: Shared/lost badges and unattended unlocked stations weaken attribution. Badge presence alone is not strong authentication.
backend_change: Routine operator authentication, badge registry, session expiry/lock rules, and named actor on movement events; the current plan only requires named supervisor corrections.
